# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**Scope:** Migrate 40,000 existing users from legacy billing system ("Old") to new billing system ("New"). Both systems remain operational in parallel throughout the rollout, enabling real-time comparison and fast rollback per user/cohort.

---

## Guiding Principles

- Migration is reversible at the user level until final sign-off (dual-write/dual-read window per cohort).
- No cohort advances until the prior cohort has passed its exit criteria and soaked for a minimum observation window.
- Old system stays fully operational and authoritative-capable until at least 30 days after the last user cohort completes migration, and its decommissioning is handled as a **separate, later initiative** — not part of this rollout's final phase.

---

## Phase 1 — Canary (2% of users, ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, refunds, tax calculation, and dunning workflows; on-call rotation and rollback tooling (single-user and single-cohort revert) are confirmed working in a game-day drill.

**Cohort selection:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, standard payment methods, monthly — not annual — billing cycles).

**Activities:**
- Enable dual-write (transactions written to both Old and New) for the cohort; New is shadow/non-authoritative.
- Run nightly reconciliation jobs comparing invoices, balances, and payment states between systems.
- Manual review of every discrepancy.

**Soak time:** Minimum 7 days before advancing.

---

## Phase 2 — Early Adopters (15% of users, ~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full soak period with zero unresolved critical discrepancies (see halt metric below) and reconciliation mismatch rate stayed under 0.1% for 3 consecutive days; rollback of Phase 1 cohort has been tested at least once without data loss.

**Cohort selection:** Broader mix of plan types (monthly + annual), but excluding highest-ARR enterprise accounts and any accounts with active billing disputes or pending chargebacks.

**Activities:**
- New system becomes authoritative for this cohort (source of truth for new charges); Old continues shadow-writing for comparison and safety net.
- Expand automated reconciliation to cover proration, credits, and refund edge cases.
- Enable customer-facing billing pages/invoices sourced from New for this cohort; support team briefed and staffed for elevated ticket volume.

**Soak time:** Minimum 10 days before advancing.

---

## Phase 3 — General Availability (60% of users, ~24,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained payment failure rate delta (New vs. Old, like-for-like) within ±0.5 percentage points for 7 consecutive days, support ticket volume attributable to billing did not exceed 1.5x the pre-migration baseline, and finance has signed off on revenue reconciliation for Phase 2 cohorts.

**Cohort selection:** Remaining standard accounts, migrated in waves of ~5,000/day to preserve rollback granularity and support capacity, ordered roughly by ascending account complexity.

**Activities:**
- New is authoritative; Old shifts to read-only shadow/audit mode for this cohort.
- Daily automated reconciliation reports to finance and engineering.
- Wave-by-wave go/no-go check before releasing the next wave.

**Soak time:** Minimum 14 days after the last wave before proceeding to Phase 4.

---

## Phase 4 — High-Complexity & Final Batch (23% of users, ~9,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 completed in full with cumulative billing-related revenue variance under 0.1% of total processed revenue, and a dedicated migration runbook has been built and reviewed for each high-complexity segment (enterprise contracts, multi-entity accounts, custom tax/discount arrangements, accounts in active dispute).

**Cohort selection:** Enterprise accounts, custom-contract accounts, accounts with legal/compliance holds, and any accounts previously excluded or deferred from earlier phases.

**Activities:**
- White-glove migration with named account owner and account manager notification/sign-off per enterprise customer.
- New is authoritative; Old remains fully running in parallel as a warm standby and audit source (not disabled, not decommissioned).
- Post-migration reconciliation window of 30 days with both systems live before any decommissioning discussion begins as a separate follow-on project.

**Soak time:** Minimum 30 days of dual-system operation before Old is even considered for retirement planning, which is explicitly out of scope for this rollout plan.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

- **Primary halt metric:** If the daily invoice/payment reconciliation mismatch rate between Old and New exceeds **0.5%** of transactions in any 24-hour period for the active cohort, the rollout is halted immediately, no further users are migrated, and the current wave is triaged before any resumption decision.
- **Secondary halt metric:** If payment failure rate (declines/errors) for the New system exceeds the Old system's baseline failure rate by more than **1.0 percentage point** over any rolling 24-hour window, halt.
- **Tertiary halt metric:** If P1/P2 billing-related support tickets exceed **150 per day** (roughly 2x historical baseline) for 2 consecutive days, halt and reassess.

---

## Risks

RISK: Reconciliation logic itself has bugs, masking true discrepancies between Old and New | Independently validate reconciliation job outputs against a manually audited sample each phase; peer-review reconciliation code before Phase 1 | Data Engineering Lead
RISK: Duplicate or double-charging customers during dual-write window | Implement idempotency keys and transaction-id cross-referencing between systems; automated alert on any duplicate charge detected within 5 minutes | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers in Phase 4 experience contract-term or invoice discrepancies causing revenue leakage or customer disputes | Require dedicated account manager sign-off and a dry-run invoice comparison per enterprise account before cutover | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a phase, delaying detection of systemic issues | Pre-scale support staffing per phase based on cohort size and establish a dedicated billing-migration escalation queue | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback of a cohort from New back to Old fails or causes data loss under real production load | Run a full rollback game-day rehearsal before each phase and require a tested, timestamped rollback runbook as an entry criterion | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Regulatory/tax calculation differences between systems cause under- or over-collection of tax | Run parallel tax-calculation audits with the tax/compliance team for every cohort before it goes authoritative on New | Finance & Compliance Lead

PHASES: 4
